subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which chord progression?
questions.explain: A perfect cadence moves from chord V to chord I, sounding finished.

questions.q: A 'click track' used when recording provides:
options: A guide beat to keep performers in time
questions.explain: A click track is a steady metronome beat in the headphones that keeps performers in time while recording.

questions.q: Which term refers to the tone quality or 'colour' of a sound that lets you tell a flute from a violin?
questions.explain: Timbre, or sonority, is the characteristic tone colour that distinguishes one instrument or voice from another.

questions.q: What does 'rit.' (ritardando) mean?
questions.explain: Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: On a string instrument, the technique 'pizzicato' means to:
options: Pluck the strings with the finger
questions.explain: Pizzicato instructs the player to pluck the strings rather than bow them.

questions.q: Which time signature is an example of compound time?
questions.explain: 6/8 is compound time because each beat divides into three quavers (two dotted-crotchet beats).

questions.q: A minim is worth how many crotchet beats?
questions.explain: A minim is worth two crotchet beats.

questions.q: Which structure follows the pattern ABA?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in an ABA pattern, where the A material returns.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: In the circle of fifths, how many sharps are in the key signature of D major?
questions.explain: D major has two sharps (F sharp and C sharp) in its key signature.

questions.q: 'Sight-reading' means:
options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.

questions.q: What is 'syncopation'?
options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: 'Composing to a brief' means:
options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a metronome when practising a performance?
options: It helps you keep a steady, accurate tempo
questions.explain: A metronome sounds a steady beat, helping a performer keep an accurate and consistent tempo.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: What does a natural sign do?
options: Raises a note by a tone
Cancels a previous sharp or flat
Lowers a note by a tone
questions.explain: A natural cancels a sharp or flat, returning the note to its natural pitch.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: In music technology, 'panning' a sound controls:
options: Its position between the left and right speakers
questions.explain: Panning places a sound in the stereo field, between the left and right speakers.

questions.q: The interval of an octave between two notes of the same letter name spans how many semitones?
questions.explain: An octave spans twelve semitones from one note to the next of the same name.

questions.q: Which cadence creates a surprise by moving from chord V to chord VI instead of I?
questions.explain: An interrupted cadence moves from V to VI, surprising the listener who expects a perfect cadence.
